principles.label: Barometric pressure
principles.rule: Fish respond to pressure change: high pressure tends to produce feeding while low pressure sends fish to cover ahead of bad weather; the feed is often strongest just before a front and returns a few days after the pressure rises, while dramatic swings can shut fishing off.

citations.source: Take Me Fishing (RBFF) — The Best Time to Fish? Read the Weather (July 2016)
citations.quote: High pressure, fish eat, low pressure, fish take cover due to impending bad weather.

principles.label: Solunar periods
principles.rule: Solunar theory holds that animals move with the moon's position: major periods occur when the moon is overhead or underfoot, minor periods at moonrise and moonset, and activity is strongest around the new and full moon — conditional on stable weather and water.

citations.claim: solunar theory: fish and animals move with the moon's position
citations.quote: The solunar theory is a hypothesis that fish and other animals move according to the location of the moon in comparison to their bodies.
